explanation: Kissing or hugging in public can be prosecuted in the UAE as an offence against public decency — a British couple was jailed in 2010 after being convicted of kissing in a Dubai restaurant — though enforcement is inconsistent and married couples holding hands is generally tolerated. Unmarried couples carry the most legal exposure, and norms are visibly more relaxed inside international hotels and licensed venues than in public spaces.
local_tip: Save kissing, hugging, or extended hand-holding for private settings, and don't assume tourist zones are exempt from the law.
regional_note: Sharjah enforces stricter public-decency and dress rules than Dubai, including a ban on alcohol, which makes PDA there a higher-risk choice.

also_check.note: Public displays of affection are explicitly listed as a finable offence under the 2019 Public Decency Regulations.
Cheek-kissing as a greeting and casual affection in public are widely accepted.
Public affection is uncommon and can draw uncomfortable looks, even among young couples.
